title: Describe a book with C#
summary: Use C# models for book replies and incoming requests. Learn how validation stops empty or overlong titles before they reach Oracle.
introduction: When two people exchange a form, both need to agree on its boxes. Our API needs the same kind of agreement. One C# type describes a saved book. A second type describes the values a visitor may send.
learningObjectives: Explain why a save request has no ID
Use title validation and boolean values

blocks.title: ReadingListApi/Models/Book.cs

blocks.text: A **record** is a short way to describe a group of values. Id is a long, a whole-number type large enough for our ten-digit Oracle IDs. Title is a string, or text. IsRead is a bool, which can be true or false.
C# uses names such as IsRead. The web API writes them as isRead in JSON. Oracle stores the same idea in the is_read column as 0 or 1. The repository translates between those forms.
The request a visitor may send

blocks.title: ReadingListApi/Models/SaveBookRequest.cs

blocks.text: **Required** checks that a title is present and is not only spaces. **StringLength** limits it to 120 characters. These marks above a property are called attributes. They give .NET instructions about the value.

The request has no Id. Oracle makes that number when a row is created. To edit a book, the caller puts the existing ID in the web address instead. The code trims spaces from a valid title before saving it.

rows: There is a title and a real boolean.
A title made only of spaces is missing.
The text yes is not a JSON boolean.
Leaving out isRead gives its default value, false.
blocks.caption: Try valid and invalid requests

blocks.title: Check on the server too
blocks.text: A browser can check a form, but a caller can send a request without using that form. Server validation is still needed. The database rules add another check.
Write one valid JSON request for a made-up book. Then change isRead to the text "yes" and predict the response: HTTP 400 means the request is not valid.
